sentences: `add`, `sub`, `smin/umin`, `smax/umax`, `and`, `or`, `xor`, `swap` and `cmpswap` at the `global_load/store` address (same `Gen.global_address`: saddr pair plus zero-extended vaddr, or a 64-bit vaddr with `off`, plus the signed 12-bit offset), as one `OpAtomic*` on the PhysicalStorageBuffer dword, device scope, guarded so inactive lanes don't touch memory.

`fmin` and `fmax` (32-bit float) lower to a structured `OpAtomicCompareExchange` CAS loop using GLSL.std.450 `NMin`/`NMax` (no Vulkan float-atomic extension needed; NaN returns the non-NaN operand, `-0.0 < +0.0`).

`inc` and `dec` (32-bit unsigned wrapping against `DATA`: `inc` gives `(M >= DATA) ? 0 : M + 1`, `dec` gives `(M == 0 || M > DATA) ? DATA : M - 1`, RDNA2 ISA) also lower to a structured `OpAtomicCompareExchange` CAS loop via `Gen.atomic_inc_dec_cas` for both `global_atomic_{inc,dec}` and MUBUF `buffer_atomic_{inc,dec}` (preserving MUBUF bounds checks: OOB/inactive lanes leave memory untouched and return 0 with `glc`).
With `glc` the pre-op value lands in `vdst`, the first operand; without `glc` there is no `vdst`, and the first-read analysis counts operand 0 as the address (a source).
`cmpswap` takes `vdata` as the pair {DATA, CMP}: `M = (M == CMP) ? DATA : M`, as `buffer_atomic_cmpswap`.

`and/or/xor/swap_x2` work on a 64-bit element (two dwords, low first) as one 32-bit atomic per dword, with no Int64 atomics: a bitwise op leaves the same memory that way, since its bits are independent.

**Approximation:** an exchange can tear, since two lanes swapping into one element at once can leave one's low dword with the other's high dword (A.lo, B.lo, B.hi, A.hi), and the returned pair comes from two reads, so another lane's 64-bit op on the same element between them can show up half done (as for `ds_and/or/xor_b64`).
Still `Unsupported`: the other `_x2` forms (`add/sub/min/max/inc/dec/fmin/fmax_x2` carry or compare across the dwords, and `cmpswap_x2` compares all 64 bits), `fcmpswap`, and `slc`/`dlc`.
Until 2026-11-22 every global atomic was rejected.

CPU-checked by `tests/semantic/test_global_atomics.py` (all ten integer ops plus `fmin`/`fmax` on a value grid with and without `glc`, NaN/±0/±inf, multi-lane CAS contention, `cmpswap`, offsets from -2048 to 2044, `off` addressing, seeded values, rejected forms, the first-read analysis), `tests/semantic/test_atomic_inc_dec.py` (`global_atomic_{inc,dec}` and `buffer_atomic_{inc,dec}` edge grid, wraparound, `glc` vs non-`glc`, signed offsets, `off` addressing, MUBUF bounds/OOB, inactive lanes, multi-lane CAS contention, first-read analysis, rejected `_x2`/`slc`/`dlc` forms), and `tests/semantic/test_global_atomics_x2.py` (the four `_x2` forms with and without `glc`, an offset, seeded values, the carrying forms rejected), and validated with `spirv-val` (native and `--wave64-emulate`).
